stem: Nitya draws two angles on her slate. Angle $R$ has short arms and a wide turn about its vertex. Angle $S$ has long arms and a narrow turn about its vertex.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides which angle is larger?

options.text: Angle $S$ is larger, because its arms are drawn longer.
Angle $R$ is larger, because it has the greater amount of turn about the vertex.
The drawn arm lengths are what produce the amount of turn.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Angle size is the amount of turn about the vertex from one ray to the other, so the wider turn at $R$ makes angle $R$ larger.

teacher.key_rationale: Turn about the vertex decides size, not arm length. Treating longer arms as larger, or saying arm lengths create the turn, miss that hinge.
